audit.scope: Performance and responsiveness only. Component support, correctness, and unsupported-component work are intentionally excluded.
audit.method: Static audit of the active simulator, worker, store, and canvas execution paths. No browser CPU, memory, or frame-time trace was captured in this audit.
audit.interpretation: Each item is confirmed as existing work in the code path. Its measured contribution on a particular laptop must be baselined before and after implementation.

items.title: Make solver work adaptive to circuit cost
items.appliesWhen: Every MNA simulation; impact grows with circuit size and nonlinear elements.
evidence: SimulationWorker.ts runs every 16 ms and, with the default 1 ms timestep, performs about 16 solve passes per worker tick.
MNASolver.ts creates a dense matrix for each solve, permits up to 50 Newton-Raphson iterations, and uses dense Gaussian elimination.
items.work: Introduce an explicit simulation-work budget with adaptive substeps or timestep selection for large circuits. Preserve a user-visible full-fidelity mode for cases that require the current transient accuracy.
definitionOfDone: The maximum-component circuit has a bounded solver budget per wall-clock frame.
Simulation time remains monotonic and the selected fidelity mode is visible to the user.
Representative transient, motor, LED, and digital-IC regression scenarios still pass.

implementation.summary: Added an 8 ms worker solver budget, cost-based adaptive timestep selection capped at 5 ms, Full fidelity mode, monotonic store-side simulation time, and visible toolbar controls.
verification: UI TypeScript build and Vite production build pass.
UI oxlint pass.
Static pre-change baseline captured in docs/opt-001-baseline.json.
implementation.remainingValidation: Run the maximum-component browser regression and compare Adaptive versus Full fidelity using OPT-FB-001.

items.title: Implement real worker-to-UI result backpressure
evidence: SimulationEngine.ts documents a 15 FPS UI throttle, but a requestAnimationFrame processes the latest pending result on the next frame, so result handling can still run near the worker's 16 ms cadence.
SimulationWorker.ts serializes and posts a RESULT message every worker tick.
items.work: Move result cadence control to a worker/main-thread backpressure protocol. Keep only the latest unconsumed result and do not build or post a new full UI payload until the selected presentation cadence permits it.
definitionOfDone: The measured RESULT message rate never exceeds the configured presentation rate.
A slow main thread cannot accumulate an unbounded message queue.
Pausing, stepping, and stopping still show the correct final state.

implementation.summary: Added a one-credit REQUEST_RESULT protocol, worker-side result suppression and duplicate-request collapsing, cached paused-state delivery, and a bounded pending oscilloscope frame buffer.
verification: UI TypeScript build and Vite production build pass.
UI oxlint pass.
Static pre-change baseline captured in docs/opt-002-baseline.json.
implementation.remainingValidation: Run worker protocol assertions and a browser message-rate trace using OPT-FB-001 and OPT-FB-002.

items.title: Send only solver data currently needed by the UI
items.appliesWhen: Every posted solver result; especially costly with many MNA elements and wires.
evidence: SimulationWorker.ts calculates component power for every element and converts every branch-current Map entry to an object before each RESULT post.
SimulationEngine.ts reconstructs component-current, component-power, node-voltage, pin-voltage, and wire-current maps for every handled result.
items.work: Define result subscriptions for meters, probes, current-flow, thermal view, and visible components. Emit only subscribed values, use compact transferable numeric data where appropriate, and derive shared maps once.
definitionOfDone: Current, power, and wire-flow data are absent from RESULT messages unless a feature needs them.
The UI receives no duplicate derived map for the same measurement.
All enabled measurement and overlay features retain correct values.

implementation.summary: Added worker result subscriptions, transferable Float64Array measurement payloads, explicit AI/lab full-result demand, and one main-thread materialization path for legacy store consumers.
verification: Static pre-change payload baseline captured in docs/opt-003-baseline.json.
UI TypeScript build and Vite production build pass.
UI oxlint pass and git diff whitespace check pass.
implementation.remainingValidation: Run the UI build and add runtime payload/consumer assertions through OPT-FB-001 and OPT-FB-003.

items.title: Reconcile solver results as deltas instead of rescanning the full circuit
evidence: SimulationEngine.ts rebuilds several full result maps, resolves wire currents, and scans every canvas node to update component feedback on each handled result.
The result handler also performs repeated component lookups and writes canvas runtime properties through updateNode.
items.work: Pre-index simulation-capable nodes and their MNA bindings at netlist build time. Compare rounded or thresholded runtime values, then publish only changed component state in one batch without rebuilding unchanged maps.
definitionOfDone: Unchanged solver output causes no canvas-node write.
Only components with changed display or behavioral state are reconciled.
The maximum-component circuit remains interactive while visual state is updating.

implementation.summary: Added a stable simulation-node and pin-to-MNA index, deadband/deep-equality filtering before batch publication, O(1) batch lookup paths, and indexed result-node retrieval.
verification: Static pre-change reconciliation baseline captured in docs/opt-004-baseline.json.
UI TypeScript build and oxlint pass.
UI Vite production build and git diff whitespace check pass.
implementation.remainingValidation: Run deterministic unchanged-result write-count and maximum-component responsiveness checks through OPT-FB-004.

items.title: Separate runtime simulation state from model-change detection
items.appliesWhen: Whenever the canvas store changes during a running simulation.
evidence: SimulationEngine.ts subscribes to the entire canvas store and compares every node, wire, and property-key set to decide whether to rebuild or update the MNA model.
Simulation feedback writes properties back to canvas nodes, so runtime visual updates enter the same global subscription path.
items.work: Route explicit electrical-model edits separately from runtime display state. Replace whole-store comparisons with targeted model-version or dirty-element updates and preserve the current topology watcher only for true structural edits.
definitionOfDone: A runtime-only visual update does not scan all node properties or rebuild MNA elements.
Electrical property and topology edits still update the running solver correctly.
No simulation feedback loop is introduced by canvas state writes.

implementation.summary: Added explicit canvas model revisions and targeted change metadata, introduced runtime-only node/batch actions, and changed SimulationEngine model synchronization to ignore runtime updates and process only affected model nodes.
verification: Static pre-change canvas-to-solver baseline captured in docs/opt-005-baseline.json.
UI TypeScript build and oxlint pass.
UI Vite production build, JSON validation, and git diff whitespace check pass.
implementation.remainingValidation: Run deterministic model-revision, runtime-isolation, and maximum-component checks through OPT-FB-005.

items.title: Cache and incrementally update compiled MNA topology
items.appliesWhen: When the circuit topology or an electrical model value changes during simulation.
evidence: SimulationEngine.ts refreshMnaElements rebuilds the complete MNA circuit from all nodes and wires for a model-property refresh.
A changed MNA node count stops and recreates the worker instead of reusing a compiled topology.
items.work: Split netlist compilation into cached connectivity/topology data and mutable element parameters. Update only the changed MNA elements where possible, and reserve worker recreation for unavoidable structural changes.
definitionOfDone: Changing one supported electrical property does not rebuild unrelated connectivity.
Topology changes preserve the expected solver lifecycle and do not leak workers.
Breadboard and direct-wire connectivity regressions pass.

implementation.summary: Added a cached MNA topology contract, a cache-aware netlist path that skips Union-Find and breadboard proximity discovery for model-only refreshes, topology-shape validation, in-place mutable element patches, and dedicated scope-channel updates.
verification: Static pre-change netlist and worker lifecycle baseline captured in docs/opt-006-baseline.json.
UI TypeScript build and oxlint pass.
UI Vite production build, JSON validation, and git diff whitespace check pass.
implementation.remainingValidation: Run deterministic mutable-element patch counts, worker lifecycle checks, and breadboard/direct-wire connectivity regressions through OPT-FB-006.

items.title: Batch oscilloscope and logic-capture buffering
items.appliesWhen: When one or more oscilloscope channels are connected.
evidence: SimulationWorker.ts collects scope samples for every transient substep and posts all pending frames with the next worker result.
SimulationEngine.ts appends each frame and channel individually, while simulationStore.ts copies retained scope and logic arrays on every append.
items.work: Use fixed-capacity ring buffers or chunked batches outside the render-critical store, downsample according to the active scope timebase, and publish one snapshot per presentation frame.
definitionOfDone: A worker result with multiple scope frames produces one batched store publication.
Retained waveform history has a fixed memory bound without repeated full-array copies.
Scope waveform order, timebase, and pause/step behavior remain correct.

implementation.summary: Added timebase-aware worker capture intervals, fixed-capacity typed-array buffering, transferable scope batches, external fixed-capacity waveform and logic rings, one store publication per batch, and a step-owned result credit that preserves paused step ordering.
verification: Static pre-change scope pipeline baseline captured in docs/opt-007-baseline.json.
UI TypeScript build and oxlint pass.
UI Vite production build, JSON validation, and git diff whitespace check pass.
implementation.remainingValidation: Run deterministic buffer-wrap, timebase-change, pause/step, and protocol-decoder capture checks through OPT-FB-007.

items.title: Add a rendering-quality budget for dense wire and current-flow views
items.appliesWhen: Large canvases; current-flow animation is an additional cost when enabled.
evidence: CircuitCanvas.tsx mounts a WireShape for every wire in the canvas.
CurrentFlowLayer.tsx recomputes and draws particles for every active wire on every Konva animation frame when current flow is enabled.
items.work: Add viewport culling and an adaptive visual budget: cap animated particles, reduce animation cadence at overview zoom, and provide a clear large-circuit quality mode without hiding electrical values.
definitionOfDone: Off-screen wires and particles do not consume normal render work.
Current-flow animation stays legible without a dense visual-noise field.
Users can identify when a quality limit is active and can opt into full detail.

implementation.summary: Added viewport-culled schematic and PCB wire layers, restricted current-flow geometry to visible wires, introduced density/zoom-aware particle and cadence budgets, and exposed a visible Full detail override without changing solver electrical values.
verification: Static pre-change rendering baseline captured in docs/opt-008-baseline.json.
UI TypeScript build and oxlint pass.
UI Vite production build, JSON validation, and git diff whitespace check pass.
implementation.remainingValidation: Run deterministic scene-count checks and a browser frame-time/GPU trace for adaptive and full visual modes through OPT-FB-008.

items.title: Budget native AVR emulation on the main thread
items.appliesWhen: Only when a supported board runs compiled HEX through AVR8js.
evidence: SimulationEngine.ts runs 25,000 AVR instructions inside a 16 ms main-thread interval for the native AVR path.
This work shares the UI thread with React, Konva, input handling, and worker-result reconciliation.
items.work: Make AVR instruction batches time-budgeted, yield when the frame budget is exhausted, and expose the emulator workload in the same performance diagnostics used for the solver.
definitionOfDone: Native AVR execution cannot monopolize a frame for an unbounded duration.
Instruction timing remains deterministic within the documented emulator fidelity mode.
The editor remains responsive while a compiled sketch is running.

implementation.summary: Replaced the fixed 25,000-instruction interval with requestAnimationFrame execution slices, 4 ms Adaptive and 8 ms Full fidelity wall-time budgets, bounded cycle catch-up, ordered AVR instruction/peripheral ticks, pause/power-off debt resets, and throttled visible workload telemetry.
verification: Static pre-change AVR scheduling baseline captured in docs/opt-009-baseline.json.
UI TypeScript build and oxlint pass.
UI Vite production build, JSON validation, and git diff whitespace check pass.
implementation.remainingValidation: Run deterministic scheduler-clock assertions and compiled-firmware browser responsiveness traces through OPT-FB-010.
